body.statement: Can the handle \(\mathfrak I\) be developed into a cross-fitted procedure that gives uniform asymptotic \(1-\alpha\) coverage of \(\mathcal V(p_{BT},q)\) and outer coverage of \(\mathcal M^\star\) under coarsening at random and multiply robust nuisance estimation, uniformly over simultaneous Hall equalities and arbitrary policy ties?
body.justification: The finite-dimensional inversion theorem isolates the remaining nonregular semiparametric step instead of concealing it behind an assumed Gaussian limit.
body.gap: BaerStrawdermanErtefaie2023 supplies coarsening-at-random identification, an efficiency bound, and multiply robust estimation for the expected number of recurrent events in the presence of a terminal event; AndrewsSoares2010 handles unknown binding inequalities, and Gafarov2025 treats polygonal support functions. Their joint use for the entire threshold-value and optimizer correspondences is unsettled.
body.consumer: The answer would permit efficient use of incompletely observed recurrent-event trials while retaining coverage at scientifically important cap-feasibility boundaries.
